name: Baby Poo
lede: Baby Poo is a dull mustard-yellow named for the plain color of an infant's stool, one of a cluster of scatological names the 2010 xkcd color survey gave to this stretch of yellow-brown.

sections.title: A crowd name for a plain comparison
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Who typed "baby poo" first is undocumented; the survey records only the winning name, not its author [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a deep yellow, about 2.4 units off, with Munsell notation 5.5Y 5.9/9.0 [1].

The same vote produced several near-duplicate scatological names for close shades of this yellow-brown, including [[baby-poop|Baby Poop]] and [[baby-shit-brown|Baby Shit Brown]], each naming the same real-world comparison rather than a dye or a place [1]. The closest look-alikes in our data are [[brown-yellow|Brown-Yellow]] and [[dark-mustard|Dark Mustard]], both within 2.5 units, with [[diarrhea|Diarrhea]] a darker neighbor [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this mustard-yellow in 85 of them, about 0.36 percent, more common than 55 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 1.5 times the expected rate for that century (9 of 1,674 paintings from then), and inside a painting it is almost always an accent, 79 percent of the time, by lightness rank rather than raw area [2].

It is also over-represented in paintings from India, at 5.2 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest match in our archive is dated 1484, by Sandro Botticelli, 526 years before the name itself appears in 2010 [2]. Our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and the match is only a look-alike hue, not proof the name or a matching dye existed then [2].
